blocks.html: RQ1 — Accuracy. Conditional regression improves the inspected FX short-horizon score, while the separately fitted Treasury regression primary deteriorates. The exact additive bridge separates the joint history/update contrast from the conditional-procedure contrast, without identifying causal estimator effects. Historical, neighbor and conditional-model rankings depend on the executed comparison.

RQ2 — Evaluation. A score gain can coexist with more breach occasions, crossed elementary-score curves and horizon-incoherent fitted reports. The floor projection and classical construction properties clarify what can be guaranteed pointwise or under population assumptions; the fitted empirical reports have no automatic coverage guarantee. Score, calibration and report-coherence evidence must retain their distinct nulls and meanings.

RQ3 — Transport. Parsimonious regression, related aggregate tasks and strong implemented baselines give mixed and frequently adverse outcomes. The observed aggregate failures delimit portability across financial measurement processes; they are not independent dealer replications or proof that all conditional methods fail.

The evidential next steps are execution of the timestamped prospective public-release protocol, access to a compatible unseen dealer series, and evaluation of the remaining method classes under explicit mature-label timing. The additional finite adaptations and combinations do not close those evidence gaps. Investigator selection, downloaded vintages, unexecuted alternatives and the missing decision-cost mapping constrain interpretation. All original adverse cells and unsuccessful fits remain in the Supplement.

blocks.html: The FX input is the one-hour member of the Net Position Time Series Dataset, version 2: 18,576 records from 5 February 2014 01:00 through 24 January 2017 00:00. Wisniewski et al. (2020) attribute these aggregate client-flow positions across five liquid currency pairs to one market maker; this source description does not independently verify a complete dealer book. We use datetime and the signed NetPosUsd scalar, rather than reconstructing raw currency positions, hedge transactions or cash movements. The source has 18,420 one-hour and 155 forty-nine-hour adjacent gaps. We preserve chronology without sorting, removing gap-crossing windows or interpolation. Recorded-clock and vintage limits are collected in Section 10.

The Treasury source is New York Fed Primary Dealer Statistics series PDPOSGS-B, Treasury-bill long positions less short positions. FR 2004A supplies Wednesday-close positions at market/fair value. Its instructions use trade-date accounting, with specified buyback treatment on settlement date, and include eligible forward and when-issued outright positions; the series is not settled cash holdings (Board of Governors, March 2013 and July 2024 instructions). The accepted snapshot has 706 seven-day-spaced records from 3 April 2013 through 7 October 2026, in USD millions. It aggregates reporting dealers and can reflect valuation or reporting-composition changes. Taking an absolute value after summing signed positions permits cross-dealer cancellation: a small aggregate can coexist with large individual magnitudes (Duffie et al., 2023). The absolute signed aggregate is not the sum of absolute dealer positions and does not identify gross exposures or pure customer order flow.

Treasury validation issue dates are 24 July 2019 to 15 July 2020. The final H=24 validation label ends at index 404 on 30 December 2020, before evaluation begins at 405 on 6 January 2021. The last common issue is 681 on 22 April 2026; its H=6 label ends at 687 on 3 June, and H=24 at 705 on 7 October 2026. FX validation ends at origin 11902; its latest H=24 label ends at 11926, before evaluation origin 11927.

All horizons share the source-specific evaluation forecast origins. Horizon H counts subsequent source records, so the response uses H+1 observed positions including issue time. FX gaps are retained in chronological order. Treasury transitions follow the weekly economic-date clock. Exact data identities, access routes and reproduction commands are retained in the repository guide.

Economic dates and public releases differ. New York Fed statistics normally update on Thursday for the preceding reporting week; a 2004 announcement established a one-week publication lag. Exact historical release times, holidays and original unrevised observations were not reconstructed. The inspected API routes supplied no verified historical release-vintage selector, which is not proof that no archive exists elsewhere. The Treasury exercise is a downloaded-vintage replay indexed by economic as-of date, treating the current record as known at issue by convention. It is not a live public-information or as-released backtest.
Data sources: Lindsay (2020); Federal Reserve Bank of New York (2026).

The FX validation and evaluation segments contain 1440 and 6625 origins, with histories 720 or 2880 and scheduled refits every 24 records. Treasury contains 52 and 277 origins, histories 52 or 260 and refits every 13 records. Supplement Table S36 gives the full chronological and computational budgets.
